chapter: Wax Records, Broadway shows and Eddie Condon
title: Records with Woody Guthrie, Josh White and Mary Lou Williams
summary: Hall lists the unusual styles he has covered, including Asch records and the trio sides with Bill Coleman.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: From the symphonies, I did the Ballet USA in '58, and symphonic and jazz.
But in jazz you played with many different styles.
Right. One of my first recordings was with Woodie Guthrie.
Playing one-string (inaudible) fiddle. And Josh White --
You are on a few Ash Records.
Yeah, you are with Bill Coleman.
Same prize Surprise records, some of the first records I bought personally.
Yeah, I told you my brother had --
Gone to the Navy and among the first records I bought, that was among the first records I bought.

Yeah, that was quite a ball. Bill and I had been working with Ellis Larkins at this point and Ellis burned his fingers lighting a cigarette, the match went off in his hands, so Mary Lou Williams finished out the engagement at Cafe Society Uptown --
And during that time, the record date came about. That's how Bill and I were with Mary Lou.
